Perform fitting with full model.

Source: R/sc.p.vector.R
sc.p.vector.Rd

Performs a regression fit for each gene taking all variables present in the model.

sc.p.vector(
  scmpObj,
  p_value = 0.05,
  mt_correction = "BH",
  min_na = 6,
  min_counts = 0,
  min_bins_expressed = 0,
  family = negative.binomial(theta = 10, link = link),
  epsilon = 1e-08,
  verbose = TRUE,
  offset = TRUE,
  max_it = 100,
  link = "log",
  theta_estimate = "none",
  test = "chisq",
  BPPARAM = SerialParam()
)

Arguments

scmpObj

An object of class ScMaSigPro.

p_value

Significance level used for variable selection in the stepwise regression.

mt_correction

A character string specifying the p-value correction method.

min_na

Minimum number of bins with a value (not NA) that a gene needs to be fitted, as min.obs in maSigPro::p.vector(). It only matters for counts with missing values, such as microarray data given to create_scmp() with use_as_bin = TRUE: the pseudo-bulk counts of sc.squeeze() and pb_counts() have a value in every bin, so every gene passes whenever min_na is at most the number of bins. It cannot be more than the number of bins of the design.

min_counts

Minimum total count of a gene, summed over the bins of the design. Genes with fewer counts are left out of the fit. The default, 0, keeps every gene.

min_bins_expressed

Minimum number of bins of the design in which a gene has a count above 0. Genes expressed in fewer bins are left out of the fit. The default, 0, keeps every gene; it can be at most the number of bins.

family

Distribution of the error term, a family object. The default is the negative binomial family with theta = 10 and the link given by link. A family given here is used with its own link.

epsilon

Model convergence tolerance.

verbose

Print detailed output in the console. (Default is TRUE)

offset

logical value specifying whether to use offset during fitting. The offset of each bin, the logarithm of its size factor (see Details), is added to the linear predictor, where it scales the fitted mean under the log link only: with any other link the fits stop with an error unless offset = FALSE.

max_it

Maximum number of iterations to fit the model.

link

Link function of the default family: "log" (the default, the model of the paper) or "identity". When family is also given, link must be the link of that family. The identity link needs offset = FALSE; under it the fitted mean of a gene can become negative, and glm() then warns.

theta_estimate

For a negative binomial family: "none" (the default) fits every gene with the theta of family (10 by default, as maSigPro). "gene" estimates theta by maximum likelihood on each gene's full model and fits the gene with it; "global" fits every gene with the median of these estimates. The estimates are kept in the distribution parameter, for sc.t.fit() and plotDiagnostics(): theta_gene holds one per gene and theta_estimate the choice.

test

The test of each gene's full model against its intercept-only model: "chisq" (the default) or "F". Both divide the difference in deviance between the two models by the dispersion of the full model, which, for the negative binomial and Gaussian families, is estimated as its Pearson statistic divided by its residual degrees of freedom. "chisq" compares the result with the chi-squared distribution, as maSigPro does. "F" also divides it by the difference in degrees of freedom and compares it with the F distribution on the residual degrees of freedom of the full model: the F test of stats::anova.glm(). With the Gaussian family both values give the F test, the test of maSigPro for that family. "F" needs a family whose dispersion is estimated, so not stats::binomial() or stats::poisson(). The value is kept in the test parameter. See Details.

BPPARAM

A BiocParallelParam object that runs the per-gene fits, such as MulticoreParam(2) (Linux and macOS) or SnowParam(2) (any system, including Windows). The default, SerialParam(), fits the genes one after another. Create it with progressbar = TRUE for a progress bar. The results do not depend on the backend.

Value

An object of class ScMaSigPro, with updated Profile slot.

Details

With offset = TRUE, the fits include an offset as Srivastava et al. (2024), Section 2.3 and Supplementary Section S1.3, describe it: "scMaSigPro incorporates an offset value to the Poly-GLM model to adjust for disparities in total read counts per bin. This offset is calculated as the logarithm of size factors for each bin". The size factors are those of the median-of-ratios method of Love, Huber and Anders (2014), on the raw counts: "The size factor for each bin is the median of the ratios of its counts to the geometric means for each gene". Only the genes with a count above 0 in every bin have a geometric mean above 0 and enter the medians. The genes are fitted on their raw counts, without a pseudo-count: "scMaSigPro can directly process raw counts". When every gene has a zero count in some bin, the size factors cannot be computed and the fit stops with an error: fewer and larger bins (see sc.squeeze()) can leave genes without a zero count, and offset = FALSE fits without the offset. The offsets are stored in the Design slot, where sc.t.fit() finds them; with offset = FALSE no offset is stored.

Genes are left out of the fit when they have fewer than min_na values, when all their counts are zero, and when they are below min_counts or min_bins_expressed. Genes left out have no p-value and do not count in the multiple-testing correction; scmpResults() gives them NA. The size factors of the offset are computed before min_counts and min_bins_expressed are applied, on every gene left by the first two rules, so these two filters change the results of the genes they keep only through the multiple-testing correction.

The test of the full model is the first step of the method of Srivastava et al. (2024), Section 2.4: "scMaSigPro implements a two-step strategy similar to the maSigPro method", in which the full model of each gene is "evaluated against a simpler intercept-only model via hypothesis testing based on the log-likelihood ratio statistic". The default, test = "chisq", is that test, as maSigPro computes it for families other than the Gaussian: the statistic is divided by the estimated dispersion and compared with the chi-squared distribution, as if the dispersion were known. With few bins, and so few residual degrees of freedom, the estimate varies from gene to gene and the test calls more genes significant than its level. test = "F", the quasi-likelihood F test, accounts for the estimation of the dispersion through the residual degrees of freedom of the F distribution.

References

Conesa, A., Nueda M.J., Alberto Ferrer, A., Talon, T. 2006. maSigPro: a Method to Identify Significant Differential Expression Profiles in Time-Course Microarray Experiments. Bioinformatics 22, 1096-1102

Love, M.I., Huber, W. and Anders, S. (2014). Moderated estimation of fold change and dispersion for RNA-seq data with DESeq2. Genome Biology 15, 550. doi:10.1186/s13059-014-0550-8
